logp.method_description: The cellular accumulation of a chemotherapeutic agent is often correlated with its lipophilicity, so we studied the lipophilicity (log D) of 3–6 by the shake-flask method in an octanol/water mixture (Fig. 5b). The lowest log D was observed for 3, while 6showed the highest log D value. Complexes 3–5 were more hydrophilic in the order of 3 > 4 > 5, whereas 6 was moderately lipophilic. This lipophilicity pattern does not correlate with higher cellular accumulation or better cytotoxicity. The cytotoxicity is the highest for 5 (oxamusplatin) and also 5 accumulates the most in cells, but it is more hydrophilic than 6. Complexes 3and 5 are quite different in terms of lipophilicity, yet they are more similar in terms of accumulation in cells. Complex 6 is a stable complex with lipophilicity within the range for better accumulation, but it shows lower accumulation in cells.
